passingJudgment.rationale: The requirements collectively specify the declared history-aware recheck behavior without introducing a separate product capability.

judgment.rationale: The requirements cover conversation snapshots, finding identity and matching, recheck classification, mutation planning, freshness, and replay safety.
Owned history deterministically distinguishes initial discovery from rechecking prior findings.
The versioned normalized snapshot supplies the complete, deterministic, auditable conversation required by the proposal.
Stable owned identities cover both inline and summary findings while preventing copied markers from establishing ownership.
Unique provider-backed matching and an ambiguous fallback implement the proposed conservative legacy handling.
Rechecks are limited to owned prior identities while initial review retains the proposed new-finding state.
The four recheck outcomes require affirmative current-head evidence and reject absence, movement, replies, or resolution as proof.
The action mapping follows the proposed reply, general-comment, ambiguity, and no-resolution rules.
Fresh head and conversation checks prevent stale mutations and conservatively stop a partially executed plan.
Deterministic action identities, provider lookup, and read-back provide the required identical-rerun idempotency.
The requirements provide the provider reads, identity verification, reply and comment contracts, read-back, and failure evidence needed by rechecks.
Fresh, narrowly scoped installation-token behavior preserves the provider-authentication invariant required for every run.
Exact-head posting and provider read-back preserve the initial-review behavior on which later rechecks depend.
Provider-verified App identity is the minimum reliable basis for ownership and loop prevention.
All REST history surfaces are paginated to completion and fail closed when completeness cannot be established.
Independent thread and comment pagination supplies exposed resolution state while preserving unknown state for incomplete data.
The provider reply contract targets only a validated top-level review comment and rejects reply-to-reply mutation.
General pull-request comments cover owned findings that lack a replyable inline thread without inventing a diff location.
Read-back verifies authorship, marker, relationship, identity, and URL before completion is claimed.
Sanitized REST and GraphQL failure evidence makes incomplete provider operations auditable without retaining secrets.
The requirements separate classification, planning, and mutation while adding stable markers, freshness checks, status actions, and idempotency.
Separately identified inline and summary items preserve a stable identity for every initial finding.
Initial review preserves risk-based events while recheck mode uses only per-finding status actions.
Schema, ownership, head, and history validation prevent invalid or stale plans from reaching mutation.
Separate retained artifacts and gated interfaces directly implement the proposed separation of classification from mutation.
Versioned deterministic markers provide stable identities for initial runs, findings, and recheck actions.
Status actions append to owned conversations without resolving threads or editing, deleting, or relocating prior findings.
Complete-conversation identity checks skip completed actions and fail closed on conflicting duplicates.
The pipeline supplies bounded attributed evidence to reviewers and complete history and validation policy to the coordinator.
Mode-specific selection, bounded concurrency, deterministic ordering, and explicit failure handling preserve auditable execution.
The coordinator receives attributed reviewer results plus the complete recheck context needed to detect omissions and unknown identities.
Initial review may consolidate findings, while recheck coordination cannot turn evidence into an unauthorized new defect.
Initial risk behavior is preserved and rechecks produce only classifications and aggregate status.
The recheck schema enforces known identities, complete evidence-backed classifications, and absence of new findings or review events.
Each reviewer receives deterministic target-scoped history and evidence while the coordinator receives the complete conversation.
Provider and pull-request content cannot alter host instructions, resources, target identities, access, or schemas.
Existing reviewer trust boundaries remain intact while recheck work is restricted to assigned prior findings.
The registry requirements add bounded host-owned recheck resources, protect them from provider shadowing, and bind validated assignments to retained evidence.
Agent views expose only declared host-owned resources and prevent repository or provider content from shadowing them.
The symbolic contract distinguishes bounded reviewer inputs from complete coordinator-only history and targets.
Head, conversation, assignment, and resource digests make retained recheck inputs deterministic and auditable without copying sensitive content.
Versioned validation and deterministic bounds prevent truncated resources from losing required target identities or relationships.
The requirements apply existing exclusions only to derived reviewer views while preserving complete authoritative history and target ownership.
Existing path classifications reduce file-scoped reviewer history without withholding assigned safety evidence.
Filtering leaves the canonical snapshot authoritative for audit, freshness, ownership, matching, validation, and idempotency.
A deterministic identity-and-rule manifest makes derived filtering auditable without copying provider-authored text.
Filtering changes assigned evidence only and cannot create or reinterpret a recheck target.
